title: The variance of one fair die

prereqs.why: The computational formula $\Var(X) = \E[X^2] - (\E[X])^2$ is the route.
Both terms are expectations and have to be computed separately.

statement:
Let $X$ be the result of one roll of a fair six-sided die, so $X$ takes each of $1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6$ with probability $\tfrac16$.

What is $\Var(X)$? Give the exact value as a fraction.
hints: $\Var(X) = \E[X^2] - (\E[X])^2$. Work out the two expectations separately and write both down before subtracting.

payload.prompt: The variance of one fair die.
payload.label: $\Var(X) =$
payload.syntax: A fraction or an expression. 91/6 - (7/2)^2 is read and worked out exactly.
